about: Settings for the request advisor (src/skills/advisor/): the conversation on an 'Add a data source' request. Code reads the person's message, decides what it is about, and answers only from what the request already holds (quoted facts, fit verdicts, test results, the reasons a step failed). It never states a fact that has no quote behind it, never handles a key, and never works around a refusal. When the request holds no answer, it offers to look one up on the provider's own pages; the model then picks a passage and code checks the words are on the page.

topics.label: who can sign up and what it asks for

diagnoses.cause: The API key is not in .env under the name the connection expects.
check: Create the key on the provider's own site (the sign-up link is on this page).
Add one line to .env: NAME=your-key, using the exact name shown under Key.
WordBench checks the name only; it never reads or shows the value.
The key may be mistyped, expired, or not yet activated: some providers activate keys after an email confirmation or a delay.
The key may be sent in the wrong place: compare the header or parameter name under Key with the provider's authentication page.
If the authentication method was not backed by a quote from the docs, it was a guess: treat it as the most likely cause.

diagnoses.cause: The provider understood the request but refused it (HTTP 403).
check: Your plan may not include this endpoint, or the account may still be awaiting approval.
Some providers ask you to accept terms or confirm a purpose in your account before any call works.
WordBench never works around a refusal: the fix is on the provider's side or in your account.

diagnoses.cause: The address called does not exist (HTTP 404): the base address or the test endpoint is wrong.
check: When no official specification file was found, the endpoints were drafted from the docs and may be wrong.
Find the provider's API reference page and try again naming it: Add a data source, with the API's name and that page's address.
Or write the base address and one endpoint by hand when you name the API.

diagnoses.cause: The provider is limiting how often it is called (HTTP 429).
check: Wait and run the tests again later.
Check the provider's stated limit against the limits on this page, and lower them if needed.
WordBench never works around a rate limit.

diagnoses.cause: The provider's server failed (HTTP 5xx). This is usually temporary and not caused by the setup.
check: Check the provider's status page if it has one.
Run the tests again later.

diagnoses.match: timeout|timed out|connecterror|connect error|getaddrinfo|gaierror|name or service not known|could not resolve|nodename
diagnoses.cause: The provider's server could not be reached: the address did not resolve, or the connection timed out.
check: The host name may be wrong (drafted from the docs), or the service may have moved.
Your own network or a firewall may be blocking it.
Try again later; if it keeps failing, the address is the likely problem.

diagnoses.cause: A secure connection could not be set up (a certificate problem).
check: WordBench only connects over verified HTTPS and will not skip the check.
The host may be wrong, or the provider's certificate may be misconfigured.

diagnoses.cause: The address points to a private or local network, which WordBench never calls.
check: Data sources must be public internet services. A local or company-internal service cannot be added here.

diagnoses.cause: The test call returned something other than data, usually a web page (a login page, an error page or documentation).
check: The endpoint may be a page for people rather than the API itself.
The API may need a header that asks for JSON, or a different base address.

diagnoses.cause: The provider signs in with OAuth (a client ID and secret exchanged for a token), which WordBench cannot connect yet.
check: This is a missing capability in WordBench, not a mistake in your setup.
Until OAuth support is added, look for an alternative that uses a simple key, or none.

diagnoses.match: could not be drafted|no usable spec|draft|manifest|no endpoints|validation error
diagnoses.cause: WordBench could not work out how to connect from the documentation: no official specification file was found, and the local model's draft did not pass the checks.
check: This is a limit of the local model, not of the API: it often cannot read a long reference page into exact endpoints.
Name the API again with the address of its API reference page (not its home page), or of its OpenAPI or Swagger file if it publishes one.
Or write the base address and one endpoint by hand when you name the API.

diagnoses.match: no usable candidates|no integrable candidate|no api could be connected|none of the apis
diagnoses.cause: No API that could be connected was found for this brief.
check: A broader need, or fewer must-haves in the brief, finds more candidates.
If you know a provider, name it with the address of its documentation.

diagnoses.cause: The test found the key in what would be stored, so the connection was not activated.
check: The API echoes the key back, or puts it in the address. WordBench will not store a key, so this source cannot be activated as it is.

diagnoses.cause: A model call failed while reading the documentation.
check: This is a local-model limit: the model returned output that did not fit the expected shape.
Trying again often works; Power mode, if set up, uses a stronger model for this step.

look_up.about: Look an answer up on the provider's own site: a web search limited to its domain, then its pages are read; the model picks the passage that answers, and code keeps it only if the words are on the page.
